text: Backend: stop writing phase files from the read path
description: readPhaseFile (server.ts) re-derives childPhaseIds from every phase file's .parent (an O(n) directory scan per phase read, so O(n^2) for listPhases) and silently rewrites the parent with writePhase(..., emitChange=false). Race: phase.update writes the old parent without the moved phase before writing the moved phase's new .parent; a read of the old parent in that window re-adds the phase and persists it, so it ends up under both parents, and clients never get a push for that write. Fix: trust stored childPhaseIds when present; derive only in memory for legacy files without childPhaseIds; move orphan/parent-mismatch repair into fixConsistency (like migrateAimFiles for aims).

status.comment: readPhaseFile, listPhases and readProjectMeta trust stored childPhaseIds/rootPhaseIds and only derive from .parent in memory for legacy files lacking the field; none of them write (readProjectMeta still persists a first-time repoId). New reconcilePhaseTree (server.ts) does the old drop-stale/append-missing repair explicitly with change events, run from project.fixConsistency. Also removes the per-read directory scan for non-legacy phases.

reflection: Verified: backend vitest 76/76. Includes a new regression test that writes the mid-move state (old parent without the child, child still pointing at it), then does phase.get + phase.list and asserts the old parent file stays unchanged. The two legacy-migration tests now assert reads don't write and fixConsistency persists. tsc clean. A read-only drift scan of the live .bowman found 34 phases with 0 parent/child mismatches, so trusting stored lists changes nothing for current data.
